analysis.investment_thesis: JK Paper fails both legs of the Magic Formula — ROIC of ~8.6% is well below the 20% threshold and earnings yield of ~10.7% (EBIT ₹928 Cr / EV ~₹8,662 Cr) falls short of the 12% minimum, reflecting a capital-intensive commodity business with collapsing margins. The 2023 super-cycle peak obscures structurally weak returns that are unacceptable by Magic Formula standards.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 11.9% over 9 years shows decent top-line compounding
Debt reduction from ₹3,137 Cr (2022) to ₹1,885 Cr (2025) — improving balance sheet
Promoter holding of 52.94% and OCF positive all 5 years provide some downside cushion
key_risks: EBIT collapsed 54% — from ₹2,012 Cr (2023) to ₹928 Cr (2025) — exposing deep cyclicality
ROIC ~8.6% and ROE 7.04% are structurally below cost of capital, destroying value over time
Commodity paper market offers no pricing power — margins hostage to pulp costs and demand cycles
red_flags: Operating margin cratered to 4.55% in 2025 from ~31% in 2023 — not a durable business
Free cash flow fell from ₹1,552 Cr (2023) to ₹365 Cr (2025) — earnings quality deteriorating fast
Net profit down 66% YoY (₹1,133 Cr → ₹412 Cr) while trailing P/E sits at 25.4x — very expensive on current earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on JK Paper: EV = Market Cap ₹6,805 Cr + Net Debt ₹1,857 Cr = ~₹8,662 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income) 2025 = ₹928 Cr. Earnings Yield = 10.7% — just below the 12% threshold. ROIC using reported ROCE = 8.63%, far below the 20% minimum I require. This is a double-failure on the Magic Formula. Paper manufacturing is precisely the kind of capital-intensive, commodity-like business the formula is designed to avoid — high fixed assets, cyclical pricing, no durable competitive advantage.

The 2023 data is a mirage: EBITDA of ₹2,108 Cr and net profit of ₹1,208 Cr were driven by a post-COVID paper price supercycle, not structural moat. By 2025, EBITDA collapsed to ₹970 Cr (−54%) and net profit to ₹412 Cr (−66%) as prices normalized. The forward P/E of 7.64 implies ~₹890 Cr in projected earnings — optimistic given current margin pressure. Even if that recovery materializes, ROIC would still be sub-15% in a best-case scenario. I need businesses earning 25%+ ROIC that I can buy cheaply. JK Paper offers neither quality nor sufficient cheapness.
